text:
jess: Heads-up — sample-app edge build fails with our TS types. Generics stop inferring and lots of `any` shows up at call sites. Happening only when targetting edge ESM bundle.

sam: do you have the exact error? is it at callsite or during emit?

jess: at callsite. e.g. `const c = createClient({ baseUrl, auth: token })` then `c.predict<'Foo'>(...)` inference becomes `any`. Also `TS6059` about rootDir when bundling.

nina: I've seen inference lose when overloads + default generics mix with `unknown` unions. Are you using positional overloads (auth first) or object param?

jess: positional overloads. we kept them for DX (nice short call) but edge + esbuild seem to pick the second overload.

tyler: positional overloads are fragile. TS resolves overloads top->bottom and picks first matching signature at the call site. If middleware mutates opts (adding a private symbol) d.ts may show intersections and widen. Recommend single-object param: `createClient<T = unknown>(opts: ClientOpts<T>)`.

sam: if breaking change is hard, try these non-breaking options: add a branded param type to make the intended overload unambiguous, or add a tiny discriminant. e.g. `type AuthMarker = string & { __auth?: never }` then `request(auth: AuthMarker, opts?: ...)`.

nina: also check tsconfig in sample-app. For edge we want: `module: "ESNext"`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, `target: "ES2020"`, and `skipLibCheck: true` to avoid lib noise. `esModuleInterop` should be false for ESM packages.

jess: our sample-app tsconfig had `module: "CommonJS"` which esbuild ignored but TS checked types against. Changed to ESNext and things improved but inference still busted.

tyler: package.json exports/types matter. If you ship both CJS and ESM ensure declarations are consistent. Consider an explicit `exports` with `types` subpath and `typesVersions` for TS consumers. Example snippet: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
},
"typesVersions": {
  ">=4.5": { "*": ["dist/types/index.d.ts"] }
}
```

sam: another common pitfall: `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` vs `esModuleInterop`. Edge consumers often use `allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true` and keep `esModuleInterop: false`. If your types reference `default` imports incorrectly TS complains in strict projects.

nina: about `unknown` vs `any`: prefer `unknown` on public generic boundaries. But if your middleware mutates object shape, keep that internal. Use a `unique symbol` key to store retry metadata so the public `RequestOpts<T>` doesn't become an intersection type.

jess: good point — our retry middleware was adding `__retryMeta` to `RequestOpts` in the d.ts via a type augmentation. swapping to `const RETRY = Symbol()` and casting internals fixed it.

tyler: if you must keep overloads, reorder them so the most specific is first and add JSDoc to guide consumers. Also add a test in sample-app that builds with `tsc --noEmit` for both cjs and esm declaration combos.

sam: minimal immediate fixes: 1) bump sample-app tsconfig to ESNext + bundler resolution, 2) avoid exported intersection types from middleware, 3) add a temporary `as Client<MyType>` at callsite if inference broken, 4) open SDK issue to migrate to object param overloads.

devx-bot: opened issue #311 on the JS SDK repo for "Overload fragility with edge bundles and middleware-augmented opts" and queued sample-app CI job for ESM+edge builds. https://git.internal.redwood/js-sdk/issues/311 :robot_face:

jess: thanks all. I'll push the tsconfig change and the middleware symbol change, add a test, and report back once CI green.

tyler: add a short note in the SDK migration guide about `typesVersions` and `exports` subtleties for packages consumed by edge runtimes — helped us a ton. :thumbsup:
